subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `openclaw wiki apply synthesis --body-file` begin rejecting valid regular files larger than 1 MiB as a supported public CLI policy?
rationale: The patch fixes unbounded buffering by changing a user-facing CLI contract; source and tests prove the new behavior but do not establish that the 1 MiB ceiling is the intended upgrade policy.

options.title: Preserve existing body-file compatibility
options.body: Replace the hard 1 MiB rejection with an approved bounded approach that does not newly reject previously valid synthesis inputs.

options.title: Sponsor the 1 MiB limit
options.body: Accept the compatibility change, retain clear documentation and errors, and require final-head evidence that operators can use to assess the new limit.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing body-file compatibility
recommendation.body: Replace the hard 1 MiB rejection with an approved bounded approach that does not newly reject previously valid synthesis inputs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent timeline involvement and adjacent Memory Wiki history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the CLI policy choice.
